title: Describing things
goal: Describe people and things by colour, size and quality, make adjectives agree, and compare ('bigger than', 'the biggest').
intro:
Most Sindhi adjectives end in **-o** and change their ending to agree with the noun, exactly like منهنجو 'my': **وڏو** گهر (a big house), **وڏي** دري (a big window), **وڏا** ڪمرا (big rooms). Others never change.

Comparison is simple: Sindhi has no '-er' or '-est' — you say 'this *than* that big is' with **کان** (khāṃ).

vocab.note: Implosive ɠ — not an ordinary g.
f سائي sāī — as in سائي ڀاڄي.
f نئين naīṃ, m pl نوان navāṃ.
Invariable; ڏاڍو also means 'very' but agrees (ڏاڍو/ڏاڍي/ڏاڍا).
Agrees: جهڙي، جهڙا. منهنجي ماءُ جهڙي = like my mother.

phrases.en: What colour is this? (lit. of which colour)

phrases.roman: munhinjī ajraka ɠāṛhī ai nīrī āhe.
phrases.en: My ajrak is red and blue.

phrases.native: منهنجو ڀاءُ مون کان وڏو آهي.
phrases.roman: munhinjo bhāu moṃ khāṃ vaɗo āhe.
phrases.en: My brother is older than me.

phrases.native: ڪراچي سنڌ جو سڀ کان وڏو شهر آهي.
phrases.roman: karāchī sindha jo sabha khāṃ vaɗo shaharu āhe.
phrases.en: Karachi is the biggest city in Sindh.

phrases.native: اهو ٿورو ننڍو آهي. ان کان وڏو آهي؟
phrases.roman: uho thoro nanḍho āhe. un khāṃ vaɗo āhe?
phrases.en: That's a bit small. Is there a bigger one? (lit. bigger than that)

grammar.title: Adjective agreement
grammar.body:
Adjectives ending in **-o** change to agree with the noun's gender and number:

m sg **-o**: وڏو گهر vaɗo gharu — a big house
f sg **-ī**: وڏي دري vaɗī darī — a big window
m pl **-ā**: وڏا ڪمرا vaɗā kamirā — big rooms
f pl **-yūṃ**: وڏيون دريون vaɗyūṃ daryūṃ — big windows

Before a postposition, a masculine singular -o adjective becomes **-e** (oblique), just like the noun: وڏي گهر ۾ vaɗe ghara meṃ 'in the big house'.

Adjectives that don't end in -o — خراب، صاف، گرم، آسان، سوادي، گلابي، جوان — **never change**. A few irregular ones: نئون naoṃ 'new' (f نئين, m pl نوان).

Adjectives go **before** the noun when describing it, and before آهي when they are the predicate: ڪمرو وڏو آهي 'the room is big'.

examples.en: She came in a new car.

grammar.title: Comparison: کان … and سڀ کان …
grammar.body:
To compare, put **کان** (khāṃ, 'than, from') after the thing you compare with; the adjective stays in its normal form: **هي ان کان وڏو آهي** 'this than that big is' = this is bigger than that. Pronouns before کان are oblique: مون کان 'than me', توهان کان 'than you', ان / هن کان 'than that / this'.

Add **وڌيڪ** (vadhīku, 'more') for emphasis: ان کان وڌيڪ سٺو 'even better than that'. For 'less …' use **گهٽ**: هي ان کان گهٽ مهانگو آهي 'this is less expensive than that'.

The **superlative** is 'than all': **سڀ کان** (sabha khāṃ) + adjective: سڀ کان سٺو 'the best', سڀ کان وڏو 'the biggest'.

'As … as' / 'like' is **جهڙو** (agreeing): شينهن جهڙو بهادر 'brave like a lion'.

examples.en: Karachi is bigger than Hyderabad. (ڪراچي f)

examples.native: منهنجي ڀيڻ مون کان ننڍي آهي.
examples.roman: munhinjī bheṇa moṃ khāṃ nanḍhī āhe.
examples.en: My sister is younger than me.

examples.native: اڄ ڪالهه کان وڌيڪ گرمي آهي.
examples.roman: aʄu kālha khāṃ vadhīku garmī āhe.
examples.en: Today is hotter than yesterday. (lit. today more heat than yesterday)

examples.native: سنڌي برياني سڀ کان سوادي آهي!
examples.roman: sindhī biryānī sabha khāṃ savādī āhe!

dialogue.title: Choosing an ajrak
dialogue.setting: Sarah is in a cloth shop in Hala, famous for its crafts, with her friend Marvi.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: ماروي، هي اجرڪ ڏس! ڪيڏي سهڻي آهي!
lines.roman: Mārvī, hī ajraka ɗisu! keɗī sohaṇī āhe!
lines.en: Marvi, look at this ajrak! How beautiful it is!

lines.speaker: Marvi
lines.native: ها، پر هيءَ ڳاڙهي وڌيڪ سٺي آهي.
lines.roman: hā, para hīa ɠāṛhī vadhīku suṭhī āhe.
lines.en: Yes, but this red one is nicer.

lines.speaker: Marvi
lines.native: نه، هيءَ هٿ جي ٺهيل آهي. رنگ وڌيڪ گهرو آهي.
lines.roman: na, hīa hatha jī ṭhahyala āhe. rangu vadhīku gharo āhe.
lines.en: No, this one is handmade. The colour is deeper.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: بلڪل! هيءَ سڀ کان سٺي اجرڪ آهي.
lines.roman: bilkul! hīa sabha khāṃ suṭhī ajraka āhe.
lines.en: Absolutely! This is the best ajrak.

lines.speaker: Shopkeeper
lines.native: اها مشين جي آهي — سستي آهي، پر ايتري سٺي ناهي.
lines.roman: uhā mashīna jī āhe — sastī āhe, para etirī suṭhī nāhe.
lines.en: That's machine-made — it's cheaper, but not as good.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: OK, I'll have the red one.

lines.speaker: Marvi
lines.native: سٺو فيصلو! اها توهان تي ڏاڍي سهڻي لڳندي.
lines.roman: suṭho faisalo! uhā tavhāṃ te ɗāḍhī sohaṇī laɠandī.
lines.en: Good choice! It'll look lovely on you.

culture: The **اجرڪ** (ajrak) is Sindh's emblem: a large cotton cloth, block-printed by hand on both sides with geometric star and flower patterns in deep crimson and indigo, using natural dyes in a long, multi-stage process (towns such as Hala, Matiari and Bhit Shah are well known for it). Draping an ajrak over a guest's shoulders is the highest gesture of honour and welcome in Sindh. It is worn with the **سنڌي ٽوپي** (Sindhi topi), a round, embroidered and mirror-worked cap with a characteristic arch cut out at the front. Both are celebrated on Sindhi Culture Day each December.
